_README: Shared test vectors for egress destination normalization. Both SDKs
(sdk-python tests/test_egress_destination_vectors.py and sdk-typescript
src/egress_destination_vectors.test.ts) run every case below, so the two
cannot drift apart.
The rule: a destination is reduced to host or host:port before it leaves
the process. Scheme, path, query, fragment and any user:password@ part are
dropped; a port survives only if it is all digits.
Why: until 2026-11-15 both SDKs dropped scheme, path and query but kept
user:password@, so 'https://alice:s3cret@db.example.com:5432/x' was sent
as 'alice:s3cret@db.example.com:5432' while the docs said credentials
never leave the process (outside review finding D13).
Every input containing SECRET must produce output without it; both test
files assert that for every case, not only the expected value.
Round 3 (17 November 2026, finding M2): 'https://host:8080/a@b' was recorded
as 'b'. A host and all-digit port followed later by an '@' cannot be told
apart from a user and an all-digit password ('alice:1234/x@db'), so such an
address is recorded as 'unreadable' by default (owner decision). A team
whose addresses never contain passwords can turn on the SDK setting
addresses_never_contain_passwords (Python) / addressesNeverContainPasswords
(TypeScript), and the host and port are recorded instead. 'out_no_passwords'
is the expected value with that setting on; where it is absent it equals
'out'.
